topic: transformers v5.21: what actually changed for local pipelines
title: Transformers pin: three moves, no drift
description: Working description; the package stage overwrites this.
hook_candidates: Transformers v5.21 landed. Your pipeline changed silently.
Three million installs a day. None of them pinned.
You didn't upgrade. Transformers upgraded itself.
Your library updates itself. Your code didn't agree.
Patch releases are safe. This one moved your floors.
Pin it like llama.cpp. Floats break pipelines.
Three moves tonight: pin transformers, sleep well.
Your model won't load. The version did it.
New transformers, same requirements file, different behavior.
narration_full: Three moves tonight keep your transformers pipeline fixed. Pin it, lock one exact version, or rebuilds pick for you. Move one: check the version you actually run. One command prints it; the newest is five twenty-one. Unpinned, pip always pulls the newest version. Move two: read the release notes for moved floors. One patch pushed the loader to torch two point eight. Unsloth's helper package caps it at five point five. Move three: write the pin, rebuild, rerun one prompt. transformers equals equals five twenty-one, written in requirements. Pin it like your llama dot cpp build tag; pip solves around it. A pin delays fixes, so schedule the upgrade. Rebuild, rerun the prompt you know. It answers like before, on a version you chose.

Entrances staggered so only one block moves at a time; each number is spoken exactly as its cell lands; four words visible at peak; cells hold static to the scene end.

scenes.narration: Rebuild, rerun the prompt you know. It answers like before, on a version you chose.

On "rerun the prompt you know" the "known prompt" node fades in left; on "answers like before" an amber arrow scales toward the "answer" node, which fades in as the arrow lands. On "a version you chose" the two-word caption "transformers, pinned" fades in beneath, rhyming with frame one's wording, no digits. Final half second: all motion stops and the wordmark settles centered; five words visible at peak; the video ends within a second of the last spoken word.

notes_for_review: After about thirty-five seconds you can pin transformers to an exact version in your requirements file, rebuild, rerun a known prompt, and say why the pin matters.
